session-circle: Equal time in and out, no holds. Adjust the pace until it feels easy; most people settle between 4.5 and 6.5 breaths a minute.
session-nostril: Close the right nostril with your thumb. Breathe in through the left.
session-triangle: Follow the marker: up the side as you breathe in, across the top as you hold, down to the point as you breathe out.
session-box: Follow the marker around the square: up as you breathe in, across the top as you hold, down as you breathe out, along the bottom as you hold.

privacy: Breath Shape collects nothing. Everything the app saves stays on your device.
This policy covers the Breath Shape app for Android and the Breath Shape website. Last updated 24 October 2026.
technique, date and time, length, rounds and results (such as hold times), and heart rate and HRV from heart checks.
theme, sound, vibration and similar choices.

These are stored only in the app's own storage on your device (in your browser's storage on the website). They are never sent to us or to anyone else. Uninstalling the app, or clearing the website's data, deletes them. You can also clear them in Settings → Your data.
No account, no analytics, no advertising, no tracking, no crash reports. The app makes no network requests about you. We have no server that receives your data.

The heart rate and HRV check uses the back camera and flash while you hold your fingertip over them. Each camera frame is reduced to a brightness value on your device and discarded. No image or video is stored or sent anywhere. Only the result (heart rate, and HRV when available) is saved to your history.

While a session plays with the screen locked, the app shows a notification with a Stop button. Notification permission is used only for that. Vibration and keeping the screen awake are used only during sessions.

Settings → Your data → Export history creates a file on your device and opens your phone's share sheet. Where it goes after that (email, Drive, a spreadsheet) is your choice, and that service's own privacy policy applies.
Breath Shape is not directed at children under 13 and collects no information from anyone.
Breath Shape is for relaxation and general wellbeing. It is not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat or prevent any condition. Heart rate and HRV readings are estimates.
If this policy changes, the new version will be posted on this page with a new date. Questions: open an issue at

entrainment: Try beats of sound and vibration at brainwave rates, and see how steady each way of timing them is. Experimental: for testing, not part of the sessions yet.

Native: the app makes the sound sample by sample, so the beat is exact to the audio clock, and hands the phone one looping vibration pattern (or composes its click effects 2 seconds at a time). No timer per beat.
Android SDK undefined Vibration motor: no Strength control: no Natural (resonant) frequency: not reported Q factor: not reported Click effects (Ticks): not supported
No flashing light, on purpose: light flickering at 3 to 30 times a second can trigger seizures in people with photosensitive epilepsy. Sound and vibration only.

The research on brainwave entrainment is mixed. Pulsed sound has some modest findings, mostly for relaxation; vibration has very little. Treat this as an experiment, and stop if anything feels unpleasant.
The vibration motor blurs beats together above about 10 a second, and becomes a steady buzz above about 15. Faster bands work as sound only.
safety: Breathe in deeply through the nose or mouth, let go without forcing it out. Fully in, let go.
This technique changes your breathing a lot and can make you light-headed.
Sit or lie down somewhere safe before you begin.

Skip it if you are pregnant, or have epilepsy, heart problems, high blood pressure or a history of fainting.
Tingling and light-headedness can happen. If you feel unwell, stop and breathe normally.

heart-rate: Cover the back camera and the flash with one fingertip. Rest your hand and press lightly, without squashing. Heart rate takes about 30 seconds; HRV needs a steady minute.
Tap the circle, then allow the camera when asked.
HRV is the beat-to-beat variation of your heart (RMSSD). Higher usually means more relaxed; it differs a lot between people, so compare your own readings, before and after a session.
